Subject: Property boundary dispute (land)

MATERIAL FACTS

1. Gopal Iyer inherited a 1,800 sq. m. plot from his father in 2012 and has farmed vegetables on it since. His neighbor, Mahesh Patil, bought the adjoining plot in 2017. Last month, Mahesh built a permanent brick fence that Gopal says cuts about 3 meters into his land along a 40-meter stretch, taking roughly 120 sq. m. Mahesh says the fence follows the "old boundary" that has been in place for decades, marked by a row of coconut trees and an irrigation channel, and that Gopal's father never objected.

2. Gopal's sale deed describes boundaries by reference to neighbors and landmarks rather than exact measurements, and a government survey map from 1996 shows the plot as a rough polygon with different dimensions from those in the deed. Mahesh's deed uses different landmarks, and one of them, a "village footpath," no longer exists. Mahesh has told Gopal that if he wants the fence moved, he must go to court, and that he will claim the land by long possession if needed. Gopal wants the fence removed, wants to know which documents will carry the most weight, and fears that years of acquiescence by his father may now count against him.
